Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own. books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp contains pipe-escaped symbol names for Rust lexical-grammar terminals (e.g. |CST-"!"-LEAFTERM|, |CST-";"-LEAFTERM|) whose embedded quote and semicolon characters a naive grep flags, but a check for true comment lines (^;) returns 0, confirming the same bare-symbol/tuple format as every other file in this rule, matching the pattern already established for a Java grammar file in an earlier unit.

grep -c for '"' and ';' returned 0 for 53 of the 54 files; books/kestrel/rust/syntax/.sys/grammar@useless-runes.lsp returned 62 and 1 respectively, traced line-by-line to pipe-escaped grammar-terminal symbol names, with grep -n '^;' confirming zero true comment lines.

review_evidence: Mathlib/Util/AddRelatedDecl.lean: Meta-programming for generating related declarations with attribute copying (lines 112-145)
Mathlib/Util/AssertNoSorry.lean: Elab command checking for sorryAx usage (lines 24-28)

Mathlib/Util/CodeActions/BinderPlicity.lean: LSP code action provider for switching binder plicity (lines 37-60)
Mathlib/Util/CompileInductive.lean: compile_inductive% command generating compiled recursor code (lines 92-199)
Mathlib/Util/CountHeartbeats.lean: Commands/linter for counting tactic heartbeats with statistics (lines 94-225)
Mathlib/Util/DelabNonCanonical.lean: Delaborator for non-canonical syntax (not read but clear from name/purpose)
Mathlib/Util/Export.lean: Rudimentary export format for Lean kernel primitives (lines 35-209)
Mathlib/Util/Notation3.lean: notation3 macro simulating Lean 3 notation with delaborator generator (lines 43-690)
Mathlib/Util/Qq.lean: Extra Qq helpers for quote4 library (lines 27-124)
Mathlib/Util/Simp.lean: Additional simp utilities for metaprogramming (lines 31-31)
